# Standup more focused on user experience (re-homed from ContextHub)

> **Provenance:** re-homed from ContextHub epic WL-0MW397N0Z002AYWP per producer
> decision (Option A). The standup skill source of truth lives in this
> (SorraAgents) repository — `skill/standup/` — which `~/.pi/agent/skills`
> symlinks to. The ContextHub copy is closed as moved.


## Problem statement

The daily standup report is currently a dry, flat bullet list of work items
("things done" + technical summaries), which is hard to read aloud and does
not convey what the user gained from the work. The output should be grouped
into meaningful categories, with each completed item described as a
single sentence about its impact on the user experience — without work item
IDs.

## Users

- The operator, who reads/listens to the daily standup (TTS) and wants a
  readable narrative of what changed and why it matters to the user.
- Agent sessions that generate standups and need clear, stable instructions
  for turning the script's structured data into the grouped report.

Example user stories:
- "As the operator, I want the standup grouped by areas such as 'User
  experience when doing Foo' and 'Back end stability under heavy load', so I
  can quickly grasp where progress happened and what each change means for
  users."
- "As the operator, I want each completed item described as one
  user-experience impact sentence without IDs, e.g. 'Improved the speed of
  user interactions with Foo by providing a one-click setup of the deck'."

## Desired change

1. **Categories** are chosen by the LLM (the invoking agent) at report time;
   labels are free-form (e.g. "User experience when doing Foo", "UI layout to
   improve access to key information"). No fixed taxonomy.
2. **Per-item impact sentences** come from a new explicit `## Impact` line in
   the work item description, written by the agent completing the work. Items
   without one (including all existing legacy items, which are **not**
   retrofitted) fall back to the current `Title — user story` phrasing.
3. **Grouped-paragraph format in every section** — "Yesterday I completed work
   on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus items for today",
   "Regressions" and "Blockers" — each section grouped **independently**
   (categories are chosen per section, not per whole report).
4. The deterministic script (`generate_standup.py`) continues to fetch and
   compute the selection data; it also extracts each item's `## Impact`
   sentence into the structured output. The LLM (agent session) does the
   clustering and paragraph rendering, keeping the script testable and the
   agent output interpretable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `generate_standup.py` extracts the `## Impact` sentence from each item's
   description into a dedicated structured field (e.g. `impact`), available in
   `--json` output; a missing/malformed Impact section yields an empty field
   without error.
2. The rendered report is readable as a narrative: it organises each section's
   items into categories chosen by the LLM at report time, items are grouped
   **independently within each section**, and no work item IDs appear anywhere
   in the rendered report.
3. Within each category, every item is described as a single
   user-experience-focused sentence: the item's `## Impact` sentence when
   present, else the existing `Title — user story` phrasing (fallback).
4. The report remains first-person and TTS-friendly (spoken-form dates, no
   ID brackets/backticks/underscores in spoken lines) and stays within the
   ~2-minute read budget.
5. CLI behaviour is unchanged for consumers (flags, JSON schema superset,
   `--output-path` write path, sync-first, commit/push); existing tests keep
   passing with additions for the new `impact` extraction.
6. Work-item completion guidance (project AGENTS.md / implement skill / intake
   brief template) is updated so newly completed items carry an `## Impact`
   sentence describing the user-experience impact of the change.
7. Testing/validation: unit tests cover Impact extraction (present, absent,
   malformed) and the fallback; a golden-output test renders a sample report
   and asserts grouped sections, no IDs, and Impact-first sentences.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, the standup SKILL.md, and any wiki/docs entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The script stays deterministic (no LLM calls inside `generate_standup.py`) —
  clustering/rendering happens in the invoking agent session per Q4 answer.
- Existing completed items are NOT retrofitted with `## Impact` lines.
- Report must stay first-person, TTS-friendly, under ~2 minutes reading time.
- No work item IDs in the rendered output.
- Surgical scope: the Herdr selection ordering and data sources are untouched.

## Existing state

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (installed to
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/`) renders a flat markdown report from the
  Herdr selection list; per-item text is `Title — user story/problem/summary`
  extracted heuristically from the description.
- Report structure: `## <project> Standup Report (date)` with sections
  "Yesterday I completed work on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus
  items for today", "Regressions", "Blockers".
- Items already carry `Key Files` and (mostly) `As a …` user stories in their
  descriptions; there is no standard Impact field today.

## Desired change (implementation sketch)

- `generate_standup.py`: add `extract_impact(description)` (parse the
  `## Impact` section) and include `impact` in `normalize_item`/report data;
  keep `format_report` as a stable fallback for `--json` consumers and tests.
- `skill/standup/SKILL.md`: replace the "Report Structure" template with
  agent-rendered instructions: cluster each section's items into free-form
  categories, render one paragraph per category (one impact sentence per
  item), never render IDs, keep the TTS/first-person rules, note the
  `## Impact` / fallback rule.
- Work-item authoring guidance: add `## Impact` (one sentence,
  user-experience impact) to the completion conventions (implement skill
  output / AGENTS.md), so future standups have real impact sentences.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/SKILL.md` — report template → clustered paragraph
  rendering instructions; source of truth `skill/standup/SKILL.md` in the
  SorraAgents repo.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — add `## Impact`
  extraction + `impact` structured field; keep JSON/fallback compat.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_*.py` — new tests for
  Impact extraction, fallback, no-ID golden output.
- `AGENTS.md` (project + `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` global) / intake brief
  template — completed items gain an `## Impact` sentence.

## Related work

- **Create a podcast for standups (WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8)** — consumes the
  rendered standup report; ensuring the grouped narrative stays parseable/TTS-
  friendly matters for it.
- Completed standup infra (sync-first WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K, maintenance
  routines WL-0MVIDWJ090090J3Q, scheduled prompts WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR) —
  unchanged; this is an output-format change.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: existing items are not retrofitted with Impact lines (fallback
  covers them). Confirmed by operator (Q5/A).
- Assumption: LLM clustering runs in the invoking agent session, not in the
  script (Q4/A). Risk: agent non-determinism → mitigations: keep deterministic
  data layer, document expected structure, golden output reviewed in tests at
  the data layer, SKILL.md instructions constrain clustering.
- Risk: paragraphs lengthen the report past 2 minutes → mitigation: the agent
  is instructed to keep each category paragraph tight and cap per-item
  sentences at one.
- Risk: Impact lines may be missing or low-quality → fallback + guidance
  update (AC6); scope-creep risk noted: no changes to Herdr selection or
  podcast pipeline (linked as related work, not scope).
- Risk: agents may accidentally include IDs → explicit "no IDs" rule in
  SKILL.md + golden-output test asserting absence (AC2).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should categories be determined?" — Answer (operator): "C — LLM-chosen at report time (free-form labels)". Source: interactive reply (round 1, 2026-11-06).
- Q2: "Where does each item's impact sentence come from?" — Answer (operator): "A — explicit `## Impact` line written into work items at completion; the script reads it". Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q3: "Which sections get the new grouped-paragraph format?" — Answer (operator): "C — every section, but group independently within the sections". Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q4: "Where does the LLM clustering run?" — Answer (operator): "A — in the invoking agent session; script emits structured item data; SKILL.md instructs the agent to cluster and render". Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Q5: "Items without an `## Impact` line?" — Answer (operator): "A — fall back to current Title — user story phrasing". Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Assumption (confirmed implicitly): existing completed items are not retrofitted with Impact lines.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRMG8P2X004V6YC** – help line for chord commands too verbose (completed)
- **WL-0MQZX8BTN006N4BF** – Automatically recover from appropriate server errors (completed)
- **WL-0MURJ0LFH002O95I** – r-i (Producer Interview) should focus on the created pane (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: access, back, category, click, completed, currently, defined, discovery, dry, end, etc, example, fit, focused, foo, group, heavy, ids, information, key, layout, lets, list, load, one, output, paragraph, providing, readable, see, should, single, stability, standup, top, under, user, using, when, you
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: access, achieve, back, completed, currently, defined, describing, doing, end, etc, example, fit, focused, foo, group, ids, impact, improve, key, layout, list, load, one, output, paragraph, readable, see, setup, should, single, stability, standup, top, under, user, using, when, you
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: back, completed, defined, discovery, dry, easy, end, etc, fit, focused, foo, group, heavy, ids, improve, improved, key, list, load, one, output, readable, see, setup, should, single, speed, stability, standup, top, under, user, using, when, you

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-06: Plan decomposition complete (plan skill). 7 child work items created in test-first dependency order. AC coverage: 100%. Key Files validated.
  - WL-0MW5HUS5E001SG6H — Unit tests for Impact extraction
  - WL-0MW5HVPJP009MVPQ — Impact extraction implementation in generate_standup.py
  - WL-0MW5HVQ7Z006SI6Q — Impact-aware report rendering + TTS fallback
  - WL-0MW5HVQY30018XZR — Golden-output test for grouped no-ID report

# Intake Brief: Ship skill triggered audits should not mark for producer review

## Problem statement

When the ship skill's release gates auto-remediate a missing/stale/transient
audit by re-running `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict`, that run follows the
**independent audit** contract and can write `--needs-producer-review yes`: a
top-level 'Ready to close: Yes' verdict that needs a producer decision, or an
independent top-level 'No' verdict, both arm the producer-review hold. These
are release-automation verification runs, not independent reviews, so the
release silently self-inflicts producer-review holds that block its own gates
(exit 9 producer-review gate, exit 12 final-validation sweep) and flood the
producer queue with items the release itself just touched. The audit behaviour
when run independently must stay exactly as it is today.

## Users

- **Producers running a release** — user story: "When I run `/skill:ship`, the
  release's own audit remediation must not set `needsProducerReview` on the
  items it re-audits — I don't want the release to block itself or queue
  spurious producer approvals I then have to clear."
- **Audit operators** — user story: "I want a ship-triggered re-audit to be
  distinguishable from an independent review: it verifies, it never queues
  producer attention; an independent audit still flags exactly as documented."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ship-triggered runs leave the flag untouched.** When the ship skill's
   release gates (Step 2 audit readiness gate, Step 6 final-validation sweep)
   or its pre-flight `--refresh-audits` re-audit an item via
   `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict` with a ship-trigger marker, the runner
   never writes `--needs-producer-review` — a top-level 'Yes' verdict that would
   otherwise require a producer decision leaves `needsProducerReview` untouched,
   and a top-level 'No' verdict also leaves it untouched (neither
   set nor cleared).
2. **Independent audit behaviour is unchanged.** An audit run without the ship
   marker behaves exactly as today: a top-level 'Yes' with a producer decision
   required still writes `--needs-producer-review yes` (subject to the
   preserved/untouched carve-outs of SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST and
   SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42), and an independent top-level 'No' still flags the item.
3. **Only the flag write is suppressed.** All other lifecycle behaviour of a
   ship-triggered run is unchanged: 'Yes' still advances to
   `completed`/`in_review`; 'No' still demotes to `open`/`plan_complete` (and
   stays subject to cascade-demotion suppression); the persisted report still
   records the verdict and a `Producer review: untouched (…)` metadata line.
4. **Targeted tests.** Tests exercise production code (not re-implementations)
   and lock: ship-triggered 'Yes' (top-level) → no `--needs-producer-review`
   write; ship-triggered 'No' (top-level) → no flag write, demotion still
   applied; marker absence → independent 'Yes'/'No' writes the flag exactly as
   today; the marker cannot leak (a run without it never suppresses).
5. **Documentation updated.** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (producer-review rules),
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (Producer-review flag lifecycle) and
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` (audit-gate remediation
   sections) document that ship-triggered audits leave `needsProducerReview`
   untouched, and that surfaced manual remediation commands (operator-invoked)
   remain independent.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Producers no longer see a release's own audit remediation queue spurious
producer-review holds that block that same release, so `/skill:ship` no longer
self-blocks or forces manual flag clearing after every release.

## Constraints

- **Independent runs untouched:** the marker must only ever be set by
  ship-automated invocations; operator-invoked commands (the surfaced
  `python3 … audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict [--force]` remediation hints
  and the `batch --strict` offline-refresh hint) stay marker-free and keep
  independent flagging behaviour.
- **No new flag-clearing behaviour:** the runner never writes
  `--needs-producer-review no`; ship-triggered suppression means "don't write
  the flag at all", not "clear it afterwards". The ship close step's authorised
  override (`wl update <child> --needs-producer-review false`, SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q)
  is unchanged.
- **No leakage risk from the mechanism:** the chosen trigger marker must not be
  accidentally set in an operator's shell, or every audit on that host would
  silently suppress producer flagging.
- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** suppression is about the producer-review
  flag only; 'Ready to close' conclusions, freshness, and gate blocking are
  untouched.
- **Repository boundary:** this repo (SorraAgents) owns both skills; no herdr/
  ContextHub change is required.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — Step 2 audit-gate remediation:
  `runAuditCommand` default runs `python3 "<runnerPath>" issue ${workItemId} --strict`
  (~line 860); surfaced manual hints at ~lines 404/536/656 carry no marker.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — Step 6 sweep remediation:
  `runAuditCommand` default runs the same `issue <id> --strict` (~line 479).
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js` — pre-flight `--refresh-audits`:
  `runAuditCommand` default runs the same `issue <id> --strict` (~line 132).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()`
  (~line 2747) returns `required` for (a) a top-level 'Yes' needing a producer
  decision and (b) an independent top-level 'No'; `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()`
  (~lines 17122–17220) writes `--needs-producer-review yes` whenever
  `producer_review["action"] == PRODUCER_REVIEW_REQUIRED`. The only existing
  trigger-context carve-out is the child-audit cascade marker
  (`AUDIT_CASCADE_AUDIT`, ~line 257): children are never flagged, and a
  cascade-demotion-suppressed 'No' leaves the flag untouched. There is no
  ship-trigger context today, so every gate-remediation re-audit is treated as
  independent.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~lines 35/38) and
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (~lines 444–542) document the
  produce-review flag lifecycle; `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`
  documents the audit-gate remediation paths that invoke the runner.

## Desired change

Pass a **ship-trigger marker** on the audit runner invocation from the three
ship remediation call sites, and have the runner consult it in
`_resolve_producer_review_decision()` so a marked run resolves
`PRODUCER_REVIEW_UNTOUCHED` (reason: "ship-triggered audit — flag untouched")
for both 'Yes' and 'No' verdicts, recorded in the persisted report as
`Producer review: untouched (ship-triggered audit — flag untouched)`. No other
lifecycle code path changes: advance/demote/cascade behaviour and the
independent-run flag rules are exactly as today. Document the contract in the
audit and ship skill docs.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()`
  (~line 2747), `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` (~lines 17122–17220),
  `PRODUCER_REVIEW_UNTOUCHED`, the `issue` arg parser (~lines 18227–18440);
  the ship-trigger marker check and the new flag/arg.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `runAuditCommand` default (~line 860);
  append the marker to the remediation invocation.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — `runAuditCommand` default (~line 479).
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js` — `runAuditCommand` default (~line 132).
- `skill/audit/tests/` — producer-review decision tests
  (`test_audit_runner_producer_review.py`), lifecycle/flag tests
  (`test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`), merge-gate flag tests
  (`test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py`); new ship-trigger coverage.
- `skill/ship/tests/` — gate remediation / pre-flight tests asserting the
  marker is present on remediation invocations.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — producer-review lifecycle and
  remediation docs.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST** — Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across
  passing re-audits; flag failing audits for producer review (completed).
  Defines the `preserved|required|untouched` decision; this item adds the
  ship-trigger context to that decision.
- **SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42** — audit_runner sets needsProducerReview for every
  medium/low 'candidate false positive' chore, blocking releases (completed).
  Extended the `untouched` carve-outs; same spirit as this item's suppression.
- **SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H** — Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for
  top-level items (completed). Children are never flagged; this item extends
  "not flagged" to ship-triggered runs while keeping child rule intact.
- **SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW** — Set producerReview flag when automated audit marks
  item as ready to close (completed). Foundational flag-on-yes rule; the
  ship-trigger context is the exception this item carves out.
- **SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G** — Ship skill invalidates audits (in-progress).
  Adjacent ship/audit interaction concern (freshness signal), distinct ACs;
  no overlap in the flag write.
- **SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q** — Ship skill: release-ready
  parent must override or absorb needsProducerReview on children (completed).
  The ship close-step override is out of scope here and must keep working.
- **SA-0MWIIOMY10054VJI** — Audit report Conclusion can claim 'Ready to ship'
  when the audit failed (in-progress). Distinct (report text), link for
  awareness.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — the gate-remediation `issue <id> --strict` invocations are the
  only ship-triggered audits.** The `batch --strict`, `check-freshness` and the
  surfaced text-only remediation hints are not executed by the release
  automation itself (verified by grepping the three `runAuditCommand` defaults
  and the hint strings).
- **Assumption — the flag is the only suppressed write.** The item wording
  limits scope to `needsProducerReview`; advance/demote/cascade behaviour stays
  (AC3). An alternative ("suppress demotion entirely, like a cascade audit")
  is recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in the Appendix.
- **Risk — marker leakage.** An env-var marker could be set accidentally in an
  operator's shell and silence producer flagging host-wide; a CLI flag cannot
  leak the same way. Recommend CLI flag (see Appendix Q1).
- **Risk — test-isolation regression.** Ship `runAuditCommand` boundaries are
  injectable; new marker assertions must keep tests hermetic (no live `wl`/
  runner calls), per the established convention.
- **Risk — scope creep into the report/metadata contract.** The persisted
  report gains a new `untouched` reason; existing consumers must tolerate it
  (it already tolerates arbitrary `untouched (<reason>)` strings).
- **Scope-creep guard.** Options recorded in the Appendix OPEN QUESTIONS
  (env-var marker, demotion suppression, marking operator-invoked hints) are
  deliberately out of scope here; if the producer wants any of them they are
  separate linked work items, not scope for this one.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (mechanism, SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ):** How should the audit
  runner know a run is ship-triggered? (a) **New CLI flag
  `--ship-triggered` on `issue`** — visible in logs and surfaced commands, no
  shell-leakage risk, matches the runner's flag-driven CLI (`--strict`,
  `--do-not-persist`, `--audit-children`); (b) an env var such as
  `AUDIT_SHIP_TRIGGERED=1` set in the execSync environment, mirroring the
  existing `AUDIT_CASCADE_AUDIT` pattern; (c) ship clears the flag after each
  remediation run. **Recommended (Map, intake): (a) — explicit and leakage-safe;
  an env var can silently taint every audit on the host if set in a shell
  profile, and option (c) fights the runner's never-clear contract.** Source:
  inspection of `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` arg parser and
  `_resolve_producer_review_decision`, and `skill/ship/scripts/*.js`
  `runAuditCommand` defaults. Not producer-confirmed.
- **OPEN QUESTION ('No' verdict scope):** For a ship-triggered re-audit whose
  verdict is 'Ready to close: No', should the item still be demoted to
  `open`/`plan_complete` (only the flag suppressed), or should the demotion be
  suppressed too (behaving like the cascade-demotion carve-out for already
  `in_review`/`done` items)? **Recommended (Map, intake): keep the demotion,
  suppress only the flag — the item genuinely failed, so it must leave the
  release queue; the release gate already blocks on the failing verdict (exit
  12), and AC3/AC1 wording limits the change to the flag.** Source:
  `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` 'No' branch. Not producer-confirmed.
- **OPEN QUESTION (manual/operator runs):** The release gate output surfaces
  marker-free `python3 … audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict [--force]` and
  `batch --strict` hints for the operator to run manually. Should those
  operator-invoked runs also be treated as ship-triggered? **Recommended (Map,
  intake): no — they are independent audits by definition; only the three

# Intake Brief: Do not require repeated producer reviews during release

## Problem statement

When a release re-audits work items (gate remediation, freshness re-runs), the
items are sometimes re-armed with `needsProducerReview`, so the producer is
asked to re-approve work the release itself has just touched. The desired rule
is simple: **require a producer review only when the audit failed for any
reason, or when code/content changed since the last review** — never because a
passing re-audit of unchanged work ran during a release.

## Users

- **Producer (operator)** — user story: "When I run a release I don't want the
  release's own re-audits to put passing, unchanged items back into my review
  queue; I only want to see genuine failures or actual changes."
- **Release engineer / automated release agent** — user story: "I want the
  producer-review flag to mean exactly 'the producer must look now', so the
  release gate neither blocks on already-reviewed unchanged work nor silently
  lets a failed item drop off the queue."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Producer-review policy is stated and enforced.** `needsProducerReview` is
   set only when (a) the audit failed for any reason (an independent or
   ship-triggered verdict of `Ready to close: No`), or (b) the item's audited
   content/code changed since the last producer review. A passing re-audit of
   unchanged work — including during a release — never sets it.
2. **Failed ship-triggered re-audits still surface to the producer.** A
   ship-gate re-audit (SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ's planned `--ship-triggered` path)
   whose verdict is `Ready to close: No` still sets `needsProducerReview` for
   the item to reach the producer queue; the ship-triggered carve-out
   suppresses only the passing/verification case. Where this diverges from
   SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ AC1 ('No' verdict leaves the flag untouched), the
   producer's stated rule in this item takes precedence and the divergence is
   reconciled (that item's Appendix Q2 explicitly awaited producer
   confirmation, which this item provides).
3. **Code/content-change trigger is not swallowed.** The ship-triggered
   suppression never overrides the content-fingerprint change signal: a
   ship-triggered re-audit of an item whose audited content changed since the
   last review still resolves to `required`, exactly as an independent audit
   would.
4. **Targeted tests.** Tests exercise production code and lock: passing
   unchanged re-audit → no flag write; failed re-audit (independent and
   ship-triggered) → flag write; content change → flag write; marker absence
   → flag behaviour unchanged.
5. **Documentation updated.** `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` document the
   only-when-failed-or-changed flag rule and the ship-triggered carve-out
   boundary (passing suppressed, failing/change still flagged).
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Producers stop being asked to re-review work the release simply re-audited,
while genuine audit failures and real changes still land in their queue.

## Constraints

- **Independent audit behaviour unchanged.** Audits run outside release
  automation keep today's flag rules exactly (SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST,
  SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42, SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H preserve/required/untouched
  semantics); only ship-automated verification runs are touched.
- **No new flag-clearing behaviour.** Suppression means "don't write the
  flag", never `--needs-producer-review no` retro-clearing; the ship close
  step's authorised override (SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q) is unchanged.
- **Reconcile with SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ before/while implementing.** That item
  is already planned (plan_complete); its 'No'-verdict suppression must be
  reconciled with AC2 of this item rather than silently shipping both.

  `_passing_audit_producer_decision()` (~line 2674) mirrors the passing
  verdict; `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` (~line 17401) writes
  `--needs-producer-review yes` when `required`. The blanket ship-triggered
  short-circuit sits at ~line 2943 and covers **both** `Yes` and `No` today.

# Intake Brief — Standup report should not use "yesterday"/"today" language, and should avoid "On [topic]…" repetition (SA-0MWNGLPD4000829A)

**Headline:** Update `skill/standup/SKILL.md` so the daily standup report speaks
in time-neutral, varied prose — "since the last report" instead of "yesterday",
"key upcoming work includes" instead of "today" — and stops opening every
paragraph with the same "On [topic], …" template.

## Problem statement

The standup report's section headings and speech rules hard-code "yesterday"
and "today" language, and the worked example opens every clustered paragraph
with "On \<category\>, …". The result reads mechanically: the same temporal
frame is asserted even when the report window is not literally a day, and the
repeated "On X," opener is a clause template the report was meant to avoid.
A previous item (SA-0MWBRJ3KI006XJ46) was marked completed but its children
were never committed — `skill/standup/SKILL.md` still carries the old wording,
and `test_skill_md_clustered_report.py` still *requires* paragraphs to begin
with "On ".

## Users

- **The operator** who reads or listens to the daily standup across projects
  (SorraAgents, AI_Hell, ContextHub, Tableau-Card-Engine, games_curator).
- **TTS listeners** who hear the report read aloud — stock temporal phrases
  and identical paragraph openers sound robotic.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want the standup to describe completed work as happening
  *since the last report* rather than *yesterday*, so the wording matches the
  actual reporting window even when it is not a single day.
- As an operator, I want upcoming work framed as *key upcoming work includes*
  rather than *today*, so the report does not over-promise a one-day horizon.
- As a TTS listener, I want paragraph openers to vary naturally so the report
  does not sound like a repeated template.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/standup/SKILL.md` contains no "yesterday" or "today" temporal
   framing in its section headings, speech rules, or worked example; completed
   work is framed as "since the last report" and upcoming work as "key
   upcoming work includes" (or close, natural equivalents).
2. The guidance explicitly directs the agent to vary paragraph openers — it no
   longer instructs that paragraphs must open with "On \<topic\>," and the
   worked example demonstrates varied openers (e.g. subject-first, verb-first,
   context-first) rather than a single repeated template.
3. `skill/standup/tests/test_skill_md_clustered_report.py` is updated to pin
   the new contract: the required section headings carry time-neutral wording,
   no "yesterday"/"today" tokens remain in those headings, and the example
   paragraphs are no longer required to start with "On "; a test asserts that
   the example's paragraph openers are varied (not all sharing one template).
4. `skill/standup/README.md` reflects the renamed section headings and the
   varied-opener guidance.
5. The change is documentation/contract only — `generate_standup.py` and its
   tests are unchanged (the script remains the deterministic data layer).
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. Verifiable
   check: a repository-wide grep for the old headings/phrases finds them only
   in the deterministic fallback renderer (`generate_standup.py` + its golden
   tests, out of scope per AC5) and in historical `standups/*.md` (never
   re-rendered).

## Impact
